problem: Rain and hail droplets erode the composite leading edge of wind turbine blades at impact speeds around 300 m/s; the erosion pits grow within two years and force blade repair. The erosion must be mitigated, not merely monitored.
Tramp metal (wrenches, bolt fragments, occasional non-ferrous pieces) entering the ore crusher damages the liners and stops the plant. The metal must be removed from the stream before the crusher.
Stochastic bubble nucleation bursts in the evaporator cause pressure oscillations and rough boiling; the process needs controlled nucleation onset, not insulation and not monitoring.
Reverse-osmosis feed channels foul with biofilm, raising the feed pressure over weeks; chemical cleaning (CIP) is frequent and shortens membrane life. The fouling must be mitigated in operation.
Seawater cooling piping suffers galvanic pitting corrosion at dissimilar-metal joints and crevices, pinholing the pipes within five years. The corrosion must be mitigated.
Open cooling-tower heat exchangers accumulate biofilm and sediment that degrade heat transfer and harbor legionella. The accumulation must be prevented or removed in service.
Slurry pump impellers suffer two-body abrasion from quartz particles; the impeller wear life is under three months at 180 HV hardness. The abrasion must be mitigated.

Gas hydrate crystals nucleate stochastically in subsea flowlines during shutdown cooldowns, plugging the line. Nucleation onset must be controlled; insulation alone and monitoring alone are not acceptable.
